speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the installation of Home Fire Alarm Devices (HFAD) for all HDB public rental flats has been completed in 2021; (b) if not, what percentage of flats remain to be fitted with such devices and when will the installations be completed; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider installing HFADs for HDB 2-room Flexi flats owned by seniors.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs whether the Ministry will consider (i) placing fire extinguishers along the common corridor of specified floors for each HDB block (ii) rolling out educational programmes to instruct residents on the locations and appropriate deployment of these fire extinguishers and fire hose reels in the common areas and (iii) forming a partnership with Resident Committees or Town Councils for the maintenance of the fire extinguishers in their community.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Government will review the fire safety standards of HDB blocks and flats to better mitigate the spread in the event of a fire; and (b) whether the policy on installation of fire-rated doors can be reviewed to allow more pervasive use of such doors.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether there is any update on the free installation of Home Fire Alarm Devices in public rental flats; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider extending such installations to all lower-income households or households with at least one elderly person aged 60 and above.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The number of fires in HDB estates continues to decrease annually, and the fire fatality rate remains low.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: MHA does not currently intend to expand the HFAD Assistance Scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Under the Fire Code, every residential unit is designed as a fire compartment to prevent the spread of fire beyond or into the unit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Fire Code currently requires fire-rated entrance doors for residential units, except where the residential unit faces an external corridor, as such corridors have been assessed to sufficiently facilitate heat and smoke dissipation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Other fire safety requirements for residential buildings include the provision of adequate exit staircases to facilitate swift evacuation of occupants, fire engine access roads and rising mains to facilitate fire-fighting operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SCDF regularly reviews the Fire Code together with stakeholders from other Government agencies, industry and academia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: An example of an enhancement would be a requirement for new residential buildings exceeding 24 metres in habitable height, to be provided with an apron wall or horizontal ledge on the building façade to minimise risk of vertical fire spread.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: SCDF has been educating residents on the use of the fire extinguisher through public engagement programmes such as the Community Emergency Preparedness Programme and Community Resilience Days.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Through these platforms, SCDF encourages residents to install fire extinguishers in their premises on a voluntary basis and also shares information on the locations where hose reels can be found in the common areas.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I have one such case in my own constituency.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I must say that MND has been very helpful in helping to solve the hoarding issue.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, I am asking whether the Town Councils can get better support from SCDF to carrying out an assessment of the fire safety every time there is a reported case of hoarding.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And also, whether NEA can also rapidly come to make an assessment of the health risk because, otherwise, by the Town Councils themselves, it is a big difficulty to try to persuade hoarders to clear the junk in their house, which Senior Minister of State Sim Ann has said represents a health risk as well as a nuisance to their neighbours.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: SCDF does not assess cluttered houses or homes, in general, to be a key fire risk.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: That said, we understand the Member and the general public's concerns and are working closely with the inter-agency HMCG to address the issue.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Would the resident know which is the lead agency that would be coordinating the efforts?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: And how would the resident know, in relation to steps that has been taken and also, in relation to the historical matters?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Because some of these cases stretch back not just months, sometimes even years.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: How would the residents be assured that the historical facts are all recorded and being followed through?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In response to Mr Murali's question, HMCG is a multi-agency effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In practice, however, it would usually be the HDB officers that are interfacing with the case on the ground and it would also be the HDB officers who are interacting more frequently, for instance, with the neighbours or perhaps the grassroots' advisor, or with the Town Council or whoever has been raising the alert in the first place.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As for documentation, within HMCG, the various agencies consulted, depending on the specific details of the case, would contribute their inputs and at the HMCG level, we will be keeping a record of all the various cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Also, I also want to take this opportunity to thank advisors, like Mr Murali, who has been following up closely with HMCG on various specific interventions.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: In view of the recent spate of home fires in HDB estates, my residents have shared that they would like HDB to review the policy around fire-rated doors to mitigate the spread, in the event of a fire.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The Minister of State briefly spoke about that.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: So, my residents are not quite convinced with the basis for the more relaxed SCDF rules.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I have two supplementary questions for both Minister of State for Home Affairs as well as Senior Minister of State for National Development.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: First, whether HDB and SCDF can work together to further review the requirements on fire-rated doors.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Two, whether residents who prefer to keep the fire-rated doors during HIP will be offered new fire-rated doors, even though the prevailing SCDF Fire Code does not require a fire-rated door.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As explained in my answer earlier, the Fire Code does not require entrance doors of residential units facing external corridors to be fire rated, as such corridors facilitate heat and smoke dissipation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The HIP offers fire-rated doors in accordance with the prevailing Fire Code.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If a unit does not require fire-rated doors under the Fire Code, HDB would offer non-fire-rated doors under the HIP.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And if a unit requires a fire-rated door, HDB will offer as such.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, the resident will have the option to change his or her existing fire-rated door to a new one, at a subsidised cost.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We regularly review the Fire Code and we work with Government agencies, industry players as well as academia to see how the fire safety aspects remain relevant, which facilitates how we can live together in our home in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: What will be the scope of this review and will it involve putting more resources into dealing with this difficult problem, not just in terms of engagement, but also in terms of engaging the hoarders and their families?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In response to Mr Gerald Giam's questions – first, in terms of the clearance of clutter, we do work together with a variety of partners.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, yes, volunteers are very helpful in this regard but also there are professional officers who are involved.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I have just mentioned in response to Mr Murali, that HDB officers are very often on the front line and they are spending their time together with MSO officers to effect the clearance of items as well.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, the key, though, is very often to obtain entry and cooperation, especially in cases where the level of cluttering or hoarding falls short of outright legal violations.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is where most of the effort is being expended.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In terms of the enforcement levers, within HMCG, we do and we will continue to work very closely first with the technical agencies, whose professional assessment we rely upon to determine whether or not a legal order can be issued.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: These are all covered under their respective Acts, within NEA as well as SCDF's purview.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I mentioned, for instance AVS as well, and that is for a smaller subset of cases.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I think one of the ways in which we can also help the officers on the ground is for there to be more public understanding of some of the complexities of the issue.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: It is very often not a simple matter of pressing a button and then the decluttering will take place.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The individual is very much a part of the picture and sometimes not being able to contact the individual or evasive actions taken by the individual to avoid anyone speaking with him or her, or gaining entry to his or her flat, very often that can delay action very considerably.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Also, the degree to which the family members are supportive makes a very clear difference on the ground.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: To this end, the media reporting recently has also been, in my opinion, very helpful because I think it helps people understand a little bit better that it is something which is not so straightforward to do, but that efforts are being expended on the ground and we will continue to do so.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have a supplementary question for Senior Minister of State Sim Ann.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have observed that agencies face extremely great challenges in getting our hoarders, especially those who face mental well-being issues to cooperate.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can I ask if there could be dedicated mental health or social support resources set aside for cases specifically under the Hoarding Management Framework, so that more attention can be given to resolve such cases very quickly?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: On behalf of the MSO which chairs HMCG, I would like nothing better than to see more resources being devoted to this issue by all the agencies that are working with us.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: However, working closely with them, we also understand that there are different professional considerations.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: It is an expression of underlying conditions which can be quite varied.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And therefore, in terms of dealing with the root cause, every case is different.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, there cannot be a one-size-fits-all approach and actually as with quite a number of mental health conditions, it is again, not a straightforward issue of prescribing a treatment.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Access to the individual, the ability to engage the individual, some awareness or response by the individual and strong support from the family members are very important, not just in terms of addressing the behavioural manifestation, in terms of the hoarding, but also whatever underlying cause could have contributed to this behaviour in the first place.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, this is something that we will continue to work together with our colleagues from the mental health sector.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Broader understanding, as I have explained earlier, would also help because then, it gives our officers more confidence on the ground as they interact with each family or household and address their responses or sometimes lack thereof in their efforts to declutter.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some cases are very complicated; I personally have come across a resident's case – after years of trying, the hoarding issue still cannot be solved.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The family members are seeking help, they are in distress that one of their family members has this habit.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I just want to find out, under such circumstances, what else can as the Ministry do?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: First of all, within HMCG, we already have a framework and as I have also shared with Members just now, we have managed to see progress in some of the cases.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I understand that Members, especially those who have witnessed or who have been handling hoarding cases in your own wards, would also like to see more speedy resolution.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is also a goal that we share.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In terms of working together with the agencies, we will seek to have intensified ground actions because I think it is important that we do the clearance, for instance, of corridors together in a more concerted way, such that there would be first, broader understanding of the importance of clear passages; there would also be some increased understanding in hoarding and what are the factors surrounding it; and also, we hope that even for members of the public who may not be living next to someone who keeps clutter, but that, when there are actions that are ongoing, when there is some enforcement and if there is, for instance, some objections on the ground from the person who owns the clutter, we actually seek the members of the public's understanding as well, that this is something that needs to be done for the greater good.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I wanted to seek clarification from the Minister of State for Home Affairs, whether SCDF indeed have the authority to carry out enforcement or issue decluttering notices to household with excessive hoarding, especially those that pose fire risks?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: If yes, is the Ministry or SCDF stepping up these inspections and issuing such notices?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: If no, would the Ministry consider empowering SCDF with this authority so that they can ensure fire safety in our residential areas?
